Tesla and SolarCity put the solar roof in the spotlight

The October 2016 unveiling puts a new face on home energy: roof tiles that generate electricity, paired with a battery for the house.

Field Notes demo desk · Historical scenario: October 28, 2016

Tesla and SolarCity are unveiling a solar roof product today, bringing electricity generation into the surface of the home itself. The pitch is straightforward: a roof can do more than keep the rain out, and the equipment for making power need not look like equipment.

The companies have placed the roof alongside Powerwall 2.0 in a wider picture of home energy. Rather than treating solar panels and battery storage as separate purchases, the presentation brings them together as parts of one household system.

The roof and battery are presented together as a way for a household to generate electricity during the day and use it after sunset.

For homeowners, the appeal of the idea is easy to see. The practical questions will take longer: installed cost, durability, performance on an actual house, and when customers can buy the product. A launch presentation can introduce the design; it cannot settle all of those questions.
